newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban punish men and women for breaking rules.
newsitem.headline: Taleban punish men and women for breaking rules.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia punished 15 men and five women for violating its strict rules on hair and clothing on Thursday, Kabul radio said.
Voice of Sharia radio, monitored in Islamabad, said 15 men had been punished for breaking Taleban rules that stipulate that men must keep their hair short and their beards long.
Five women were punished for not wearing the all-embracing burqa, a long robe that includes a cloth mesh for the eyes.
The radio did not specify what punishments had been meted out, but the Taleban have in the past administered beatings to violators of its strict rules on dress and hair.

Taleban strictures are enforced by the Department for Promoting Virtue and Preventing Vice, created after the Islamic militia captured Kabul from the former government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani on September 27.
